collect.bio: Olivier Faure (born 18 August 1968 in La Tronche, Isère) is a French Socialist politician, a PS member since 1984 and deputy for Seine-et-Marne's 11th constituency since 2012. He has led the Parti socialiste as First Secretary since April 2018 and was re-elected in 2021, 2023 and June 2025. He backed the NUPES alliance in 2022 and the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024, and negotiated a common-candidate process with other left parties. He announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential nomination on 30 August 2026 and published the book "La loi du plus juste" in September 2026.

reversals.after: Late 2025: negotiated a suspension with PM Lecornu, freezing the legal age at 62 years 9 months until January 2028, rather than full repeal. This is a compromise more than a reversal, so it is arguably only nuance.

verify.bio: Olivier Faure (born 18 August 1968 in La Tronche, Isère) is a French Socialist politician who joined the PS in 1984. He was deputy chief of staff to François Hollande at the PS (2000-2007) and has been deputy for Seine-et-Marne's 11th constituency since June 2012. He has been First Secretary of the Parti socialiste since April 2018 and was re-elected in 2021, 2023 and June 2025. He backed the NUPES alliance in 2022 and the Nouveau Front populaire in 2024. In July 2025 he helped agree the principle of a common left candidate for 2027, though PS members later voted for a primary limited to the socialist pole. He announced his presidential bid on 30 August 2026, published the book "La loi du plus juste" on 17 September 2026, and is running in the PS/Place publique primary of October 2026.

offices.office: President of the Socialist group in the Assemblée nationale (SER, renamed Nouvelle Gauche in 2017)

reversals.topic: Use of article 49.3 for the 2026 budget
reversals.before: Autumn 2025: the PS made non-use of article 49.3 for the 2026 budget one of its conditions for not censuring the Lecornu government, and obtained that commitment
reversals.after: Late January 2026: accepted that the government use 49.3 to adopt the 2026 budget because no majority could be found, against opposition from other left parties

delivery.what: Had an amendment adopted in December 2014 that enabled the single-fare Pass Navigo in Île-de-France
delivery.assessment: Cited as a concrete parliamentary achievement in his Wikipedia profile. It has not been independently assessed, and no sources of differing leanings were consulted.

delivery.what: Kept the PS in left alliances: NUPES 2022, NFP 2024, and a common-candidate principle for 2027 agreed in Bagneux in July 2025
delivery.assessment: Credited with keeping the PS in a union strategy. Opponents inside the PS, who would rather back Raphaël Glucksmann in a federation, accuse him of being subordinate to Mélenchon/LFI. PS members later rejected his preferred open primary (55.5% backed a primary limited to the socialist pole). Only Wikipedia was consulted.

delivery.what: Negotiated a suspension of the 2023 pension reform with PM Lecornu in late 2025 (legal age frozen at 62 years 9 months until January 2028), which was voted on 12 November 2025 in the PLFSS 2026; he voted for the PLFSS on final reading on 16 December 2025
delivery.assessment: A concrete concession obtained while the PS was in opposition. Other left parties criticised the compromise. No sources of differing leanings were obtained.

verify.sources_note: Sources: French Wikipedia (secondary source, no lean label) and datan.fr (primary roll-call aggregator). The session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was used up, and direct fetches of Public Sénat and franceinfo pages returned nothing usable. As a result, no press outlet of any lean was consulted. Legal is empty because Wikipedia and datan mention no judicial case involving him personally. This is absence of evidence, not confirmed absence. Traits and media portrayal are empty or unresearched because the two-lean bar could not be met. Executive experience is 0 because his posts were parliamentary, party or staff roles: he was never minister, mayor or executive president. Datan gives 92% participation in solemn votes and 95% loyalty to the SOC group. A rerun with a higher search limit is recommended to add press sources of differing leanings.
